title: A doctor for document schemas, and an opt-in pass that makes a project's documents fit
tldr: Every docs-corpus answer is only as good as the frontmatter and the sections of the documents underneath it. Nothing tells a user which of their files the MCP can read and which it skips, and nothing offers to fix the ones it cannot. Two pieces: a **doctor** that reports fitness per file, and an **opt-in skill** that reads a project's features and rewrites their headers to the current schema.
notes: Formerly item 1.4 of docs/backlog/index.md.

**Do this BEFORE 1.2.** 1.2 migrates relationships into a project that declared none; it cannot know what it is walking until something reports which documents are already readable. The doctor is that report, and 1.2 records the same suspension from its own side.

**What made this urgent.** The impact-question delivery of 2026-09-14 deleted the last reader that tolerated an old document shape. From now on a document is either in the current format or it is **invisible to the MCP, silently** — it parses, it lands in the corpus, and it answers nothing. Silence is the defect: an empty answer and an unreadable file look identical from the caller's side, which is the exact confusion `add-knowledge-discovery` already had to be taught to separate.

**The doctor reports, and writes nothing.** For every document in the docs corpus: fit, off-standard, or unreadable, naming the field or section that is missing rather than a score. `add-doc-schemas` owns the schemas, so the doctor reads them from there — a doctor that restates a schema drifts from it, and the drift is invisible until the two disagree about what "fit" means.

**The fix pass is a skill, not a codemod.** It reads each feature's document and adjusts the header — frontmatter `type` and `id`, the `## Relations` block — to the current schema. It has to be an agent reading the content, because deciding a document's type and its relations is a judgement, not a text substitution. Opt-in, and it edits headers only: never a body, never a deletion.

⛔ **The user writes nothing by hand.** Every one of those documents was written by a command, so a migration that hands the user a list of files to edit is addressing the wrong actor. The skill's output is the edit; the user's part is approving it. This is the rule the impact-question build established, and it is what killed the legacy converter there.

**Carried over from the impact-question delivery: the behaviour with no index at all.** `touched_by` answers empty in a project that has never run a close-out. `git log --follow <path>` answers it with no index and no plugin, always. Whatever ships must degrade to that rather than to nothing — and the doctor is where a user finds out which of the two they are getting.

**The open question, and it is why this is recorded and not planned.** Where does the doctor live?
- **An MCP action**, beside `search` and `history` — the agent asks it mid-flow, in the same session it is about to query, and gets the caveat before the answer. Costs an action on a surface that already has eleven.
- **A CLI verb**, `codeadd doctor` — a user runs it once after install, reads a report, and decides. Costs the agent a route it cannot take on its own.
- **Both, over one implementation.** That is already the shape `scripts/graph.js` and `mcp/` hold over one sidecar, asserted identical by test rather than shared by code. It is the likeliest answer and it is still a decision, not a default.
done_when: a project holding a mix of current-format and off-standard documents gets a per-file verdict naming the missing field; the opt-in skill converts an off-standard feature header and the same file then answers a docs-corpus query it did not answer before; no body text is modified and no document is deleted by either piece; and `touched_by` on a project with no index at all returns the documented git answer instead of an empty list.

title: Migration command: initial relationship graph for old installs
tldr: An opt-in command that builds an initial relationship structure over features delivered before the typed-relation format existed, grouped by app/group/category as a tree or graph, so the agent can find correlated features and know what to search.
notes: Formerly item 1.2 of docs/backlog/index.md.

**The relationship format this item migrates INTO is delivered, so nothing blocks this any more.** (It was item 1.1, removed from this backlog on delivery — `git log --follow docs/backlog/index.md` has it.) `2026-09-12T104012-PLAN--docs-knowledge-graph-mcp` shipped the typed `## Relations` section, the closed vocabulary (`caused_by`, `depends_on`, `part_of`, `links_to`) and the docs-corpus MCP that reads them. `templates/related.md` is gone and the `hotfix-related` schema is retired.

**Half of the migration also shipped.** `cli/src/migrations.js` migration 0002 (`harvestRelations`) walks a brownfield project's `docs/`, harvests the relationships it already wrote — body references, `related:` ids, Follow-up sentences — and writes them as `links_to` lines. Additive-only: it never deletes, never commits, and reports every id that resolves to no work item.

**What is left is the project that declared nothing.** 0002 finds nothing in a project whose documents never named each other, and that is the common case for deliveries predating the format. Such a project needs a structure derived from what its deliveries have in common — path overlap, directory, domain — rather than from a declaration nobody made.
Scan past deliveries (`docs/features`, changelogs) and group them — by app, group or category, tree or graph: the shape is still open, and choosing it is the first half of this item.
Ships as an enabled feature, not part of the default flow.
When the gitnexus plugin is enabled, the grouping also points at what to search in gitnexus per group.

**Deliberately deferred past 1.4.** The `add-knowledge-discovery` step this command consults on its first run was repaired on 2026-09-14, and the impact question — where a work item's file set lives, which is half of what this migration would have to write — shipped on 2026-09-14 (`git log --follow docs/backlog/index.md` carries the item it was). What is still missing is 1.4: this migration cannot know what it is walking until something reports which of a project's documents the MCP can already read. The usual "finish everything above before starting" rule is suspended for that reason, and recorded here rather than left as an unexplained skip.
done_when: running the command on a project whose deliveries declare no relationship produces the initial grouped structure with relationships filled, and add.new/add.plan/add.hotfix use it as the investigation entry point.

title: Treat obsolete code and backward compatibility as first-class concerns
tldr: /add.build and /add.hotfix explicitly ask whether the work must preserve backward compatibility; when it does not, they guide the author to propose a migration or cleanup script. /add.done surfaces any dead code the feature left behind before merging.
notes: Formerly item 2.1 of docs/backlog/index.md.
Add a backward-compatibility question to `/add.build` (around STEP 6/8) and `/add.hotfix` (around STEP 7/8), and record the answer in `plan.md` / `about.md` / hotfix `about.md`.
When backward compatibility is **not** required, require a migration or data-cleanup artifact (script, SQL, worker, or explicit manual steps) before the feature/hotfix can be considered complete.
Add a dead-code detection pass to `/add.done` (before merge) that lists unused files, unreachable routes, orphaned exports, or tables/columns left behind by the delivery.
Extend the relevant `add-doc-schemas` (`feature-plan`, `hotfix-about`, `changelog`) to carry the compatibility decision and any attached migration/cleanup artifact.
done_when: a feature that rewrites an existing model produces a `plan.md` entry stating `backward compatibility: no` plus a migration script path, and `/add.done` reports either `dead code: none` or a concrete cleanup candidate list.

title: Sweep the artefacts for text that informs without instructing, and name the rule that keeps it out
tldr: A pass over every command, skill and agent removing passages that explain rather than instruct, plus a named rule in `building-commands` so the next author recognises the shape before writing it.
notes: Formerly item 3.1 of docs/backlog/index.md.

The rule already half exists: `.claude/skills/building-commands/SKILL.md:583` carries ruler item 7 ("No filler"), and `@prompt-review-agent` ticks it. What it lacks is the concrete shapes to look for — the abstract test "does this change what the executor does" did not stop four instances being written into one delivery and shipped past a five-auditor review.

Name the recurring shapes in item 7, each with an Expected / Not expected pair like the other items carry: telling artefact A how artefact B behaves when nothing in A branches on it; restating a rule already stated a few lines above in different words; explaining the mechanism behind a change, which belongs in the changelog and the commit message because a human reads those once and an agent reads the prompt every run.

Keep the distinction the ruler already draws, so the sweep does not strip what is load-bearing: a scope statement (which commands a section covers, which phase an exemption applies to) and a prohibition restated at the exact point where skipping it is tempting both change what the reader does. Only the passages that survive removal without changing any action come out.

Sweep 106 artefacts: 16 commands, 43 skills and 22 agents under `framwork/.codeadd/`, plus 7 commands, 10 skills and 8 agents under `.claude/`. Product artefacts ship to users and are read on every run, so they pay the token cost repeatedly.

Decide whether anything mechanical can back the rule. Nothing in `cli/tests/` or `scripts/` enforces item 7 today, and a text heuristic for "informs without instructing" may not exist — if it does not, say so in the plan rather than shipping a gate that misses.
done_when: ruler item 7 names the shapes with examples, a run of `@prompt-review-agent` over a deliberately padded artefact flags them by shape rather than by feel, and the sweep's diff shows every artefact it touched with the removed passages listed per file.

title: Board statuses that follow the pipeline phases — from backlog to done
tldr: Replace the four generic statuses (open, doing, done, dropped) with statuses that mirror the pipeline, so a glance at the board says which phase each ticket is in and which command moves it next.
notes: **The user's first sketch.** brainstorm → backlog; add.new → refining → ready for development; add.plan → planning; add.development → doing → ready; add.done → done. There is no `add.development` — the build command is `add.build`.

**Today only two commands write a status.** `add.build` STEP 2 writes `doing` + `work_id` in one write, and `add.done` closes. `add.brainstorm`, `add.new` and `add.plan` read the ticket and write nothing — the `Writes the board?` column of `add-backlog/references/lifecycle.md` says `no` for all three. Every new phase status means one more command writes the board, so that column changes.

**Suggested sequence (to decide in the brainstorm):** `backlog` (captured, nobody picked it up) → `refining` (add.brainstorm or add.new running) → `ready-to-plan` (about.md exists) → `planning` (add.plan running) → `ready-to-build` (plan approved) → `building` (add.build) → `in-review` (build finished, PR open, add.review) → `done` (add.done), plus `dropped` off the flow.

**Suggestion — brainstorm is refining, not backlog.** A ticket reaches brainstorm already on the board, so `backlog` is the state before any command touched it. Brainstorm and add.new are the same phase from the ticket's point of view: shaping what the work is.

**Suggestion — the user's "Ready" after Doing reads as "built, waiting to close".** Name it `in-review`: the PR is open, add.review runs there, and add.done is what leaves it. A column named `ready` twice (ready for development, ready after doing) is ambiguous on the board.

**Suggestion — decide whether the wait states are columns.** Nine columns is a wide kanban. Alternative: one column per phase (backlog, refining, planning, building, review, done) and the waiting part as a badge on the card, e.g. `planning · waiting`. Fewer columns, same information.

**Suggestion — the hotfix path skips phases.** `add.hotfix` goes from a ticket straight to building with no about.md and no plan. The status set must allow a jump, and nothing may refuse a status because the previous one was skipped.

**Suggestion — every status write stays declared, never inferred, and never a stop.** The rule in lifecycle.md holds: a command writes only for the id a `ticket:` field names; a refused or degraded write is one line in the report, exactly as add.build does today.

**Compatibility trap.** `backlog.sh` writes `docs/backlog.definitions.json` once and never rewrites it — it holds user customisation. An existing install keeps `open/doing/done/dropped` forever, and a command writing `planning` there gets `REFUSED=unknown-status`. Needs either a migration in `cli/src/migrations.js`, or commands that fall back when the status is not defined. Renaming `open` also breaks every ticket already on disk, so `backlog` may stay spelled `open` with a new label.

**The internal pipeline follows the same map.** `add-plan-authoring` writes `doing` from `add-framework--build` for this repository's own board; `add-framework--brainstorm`, `--plan` and `--done` get the same rows as their product counterparts.

**The board app needs no column code.** `board/src/lib/tickets.ts` `groupByStatus` already builds one column per defined status in `order`. What it may need is the badge (if wait states are not columns) and hiding `dropped` by default.
done_when: a ticket named by `ticket:` moves through every phase status as add.brainstorm/add.new, add.plan, add.build, the PR and add.done run, each move one board write; the board shows it in the matching column at each step; a project with the old four-status definitions file either migrates or reports the missing status without stopping the command; and add.hotfix can take a ticket straight to building.

title: Add ZCode (Z.ai) as a sixth provider
tldr: Ship commands, skills and agents to ZCode, Z.ai's free agentic desktop IDE for GLM models, so a user running it gets the same framework as Claude Code or Codex. ZCode is close to Claude Code in layout and tool names; the one real blocker is that it refuses command names containing a dot.
notes: **Research done on 2026-09-23, from the official docs (zcode.z.ai/en/docs) AND the open source (github.com/zai-org/ZCode, main branch).** Where they disagree, the source wins and the disagreement is noted. Source files worth re-reading if a detail is doubted: `apps/zcode-cli/packages/adapters/src/commands/{index,roots}.ts`, `packages/services/src/skills/skillsService.ts`, `apps/zcode-cli/packages/bootstrap/src/subagents.ts`, `apps/zcode-cli/packages/adapters/src/context/index.ts`, `apps/zcode-cli/packages/core/src/subagent/profile.ts`.

**Instructions — AGENTS.md works.** It walks up from the working directory to the git root and uses the FIRST `AGENTS.md` it finds (no merging across levels), prepended by the global `~/.zcode/AGENTS.md`. It does NOT read `CLAUDE.md` (the docs say so explicitly). `/init` also looks for `.zcode/AGENTS.md` and `.agents/AGENTS.md`.

**Commands.** Project roots: `.zcode/commands/*.md` AND `.agents/commands/*.md`, scanned at every level from cwd up to the git root, `.zcode` first; on a name clash the first found wins. Global: `~/.zcode/commands/`. Frontmatter keys accepted: `description`, `argument-hint`, `allowed-tools`, `model`, `skills`, `disable-noninteractive` (an unknown key is a warning, not a drop). Body placeholder: `$ARGUMENTS`. Invoked as `/name`. A subdirectory becomes `:` in the name — `commands/add/plan.md` is `/add:plan`.

⛔ **THE BLOCKER — a dot is not a legal command name.** `COMMAND_NAME_PATTERN = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_:-]{0,63}$/` in `adapters/src/commands/index.ts`. `add.plan.md` normalises to `add.plan`, fails the pattern with `custom_command_invalid_name` (severity error) and the command does not load. Every product command except `add` has a dot. Three routes, and choosing one is the first decision of the plan: **(a)** emit `commands/add/plan.md` → `/add:plan`, and have the build rewrite `/add.plan` references to `/add:plan` in the ZCode output only, or every handoff points at a command that does not exist; **(b)** emit `add-plan.md` → `/add-plan`, same text-rewrite problem; **(c)** ship commands as skills, as codex and antigrav already do (`commands: "skills/{name}/SKILL.md"`) — but whether a SKILL `name` may contain a dot is NOT verified: no skill-name pattern was found in the source, so test it on a real install before choosing (c).

**Skills.** Project roots: `.zcode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` AND `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` — the runtime MERGES both (not a fallback). Global: `~/.zcode/skills/`. `name` and `description` are required; missing either drops the skill. `description` over 1024 chars drops the whole skill. Body truncated above 100KB. Invoked as `$name` or from the `/` menu. Only name + a 250-char description excerpt go into context per turn; the body loads on use. The scan descends into subdirectories (so `references/` is fine) but skips dot-directories and `node_modules`, `dist`, `build` and the like.

⚠️ **Double-listing risk with Codex.** The codex provider installs to `.agents/` (`cli/src/providers.js`), and ZCode reads `.agents/skills` and `.agents/commands` too. A user with both codex and zcode installed sees every skill twice if zcode also writes `.zcode/skills`. One option to weigh: zcode installs NO skills of its own and relies on `.agents/skills`, or the installer detects codex and skips the duplicate. Decide in the plan.

**Agents (subagents).** Format is Markdown with YAML frontmatter, body = system prompt — nearly the Claude dialect. Keys: `name`, `description` (required), `model` (a model id or `inherit`), `tools`, `disallowedTools`, `skills`, `maxTurns`, `color`, `thoughtLevel` (only with an explicit model), `injectAgentsMd` (default true), `mcpServers`. Tool names are Claude Code's: `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Bash`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`, `TodoWrite`, `NotebookEdit`, `Agent`, `Skill`, `AskUserQuestion`, `EnterPlanMode`, `Workflow`, `Task*`, `Cron*`. Reserved names: `general-purpose`, `Explore`. A subagent cannot spawn another. Dispatch: automatic by description, or `@name`.

⚠️ **Docs vs source on project agents.** The docs say subagents are user-level only. The source (`bootstrap/src/subagents.ts`) already loads `<cwd>/.zcode/agents/*.md` as `source: project`, stripping `permissionMode` from project files for safety. So project agents depend on the ZCode version: record a minimum version in the provider's docs, or install agents globally (`~/.zcode/agents/`) as a fallback.

**Agent dialect for `scripts/build.js` `AGENT_DIALECTS`.** Start from the `claude` dialect — same keys, same tool names, so `readonly` → `disallowedTools: Write, Edit, NotebookEdit` works as is. The one difference: `model` values like `sonnet`/`opus` are not ZCode model ids — map them to `inherit` or drop the key. The build throws if a provider has an `agents` pattern and no dialect, so this dialect is mandatory, not optional.

**MCP.** Project: `<root>/.zcode/config.json`, key `mcp.servers` (`{command, args, env}` for stdio; HTTP and SSE also supported). Global: `~/.zcode/cli/config.json`. It imports from Claude, Codex and OpenCode configs. Needed for `cli/src/mcp-registration.js` (the artefact-graph/knowledge MCP registration table has one row per provider) and for the plugin checks (gitnexus, playwright).

**Hooks — project hooks do NOT run.** The docs state it: hooks in `<workspace>/.zcode/config.json` or `<workspace>/zcode.json` are ignored in the current version. Only global `~/.zcode/cli/config.json` with `hooks.enabled: true` runs them. Event names match Claude's (`SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `Stop`). So `capabilities.hooks` is `false` for a project install.

**Plugins — an alternative distribution route worth a look, not a requirement.** A ZCode plugin bundles commands, skills, agents, `hooks/hooks.json` and `.mcp.json`. Manifest lookup: `.zcode-plugin/plugin.json`, then `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` — a Claude Code plugin loads unchanged. Plugin hooks DO run, unlike project hooks.

**Proposed `framwork/provider-map.json` entry (starting point, the command path depends on the blocker decision):** `"zcode": { "dir": "framwork/.zcode", "commands": "commands/{name}.md", "skills": "skills/{name}/SKILL.md", "agents": "agents/{name}.md", "capabilities": { "hooks": false, "agentDispatch": true, "mcp": true, "nativeFormat": "md", "slashCommands": true, "structuredQuestions": true }, "docs": ["https://zcode.z.ai/en/docs/commands", "https://zcode.z.ai/en/docs/skill", "https://zcode.z.ai/en/docs/subagents", "https://zcode.z.ai/en/docs/mcp-services", "https://zcode.z.ai/en/docs/hooks"] }`. `structuredQuestions: true` because `AskUserQuestion` exists.

**Where a new provider is wired in this repo (found by grep, 2026-09-23):** `framwork/provider-map.json` (registry), `scripts/build.js` (`AGENT_DIALECTS`, and the output dir list), `cli/src/providers.js` (`PROVIDERS` entry with src/dest/commandsSubdir/skillsSubdir/agentsSubdir/globalDest, plus `PROVIDER_PRIORITY`), `cli/src/mcp-registration.js` (one row per provider: file + format), `cli/src/uninstaller.js` (`ADD_DIRS` / `GLOBAL_ADD_DIRS` must learn `.zcode`), `workbench/skills/add-framework-product-layer/SKILL.md` (names the providers). The "5 providers" wording in `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` and the web docs also changes — `add-framework--sync` regenerates the last two.

**Feature injection and plugin agent injection.** Commands are markdown with `<!-- feature: -->` markers, so `commandsSubdir: 'commands'` lets feature injection work if route (a) or (b) is chosen. If route (a) nests commands in `add/`, check that `cli/src/injection-core.js` finds files one level down. `agentInjection` stays Claude-only today; ZCode could take it later since its agents are markdown.
**Global install.** ZCode has a real global root (`~/.zcode/{commands,skills,agents,AGENTS.md}`), so `globalDest: '.zcode'` is possible — unlike cursor and antigrav.
done_when: `npm run build` emits `framwork/.zcode/` with every command, skill and agent; installing with the zcode provider into a scratch project and opening it in ZCode lists every framework command under `/` (none dropped with `custom_command_invalid_name`), every skill under `$`, and every agent under `@`; a handoff line inside a command names a command that actually exists in that install; a project with codex and zcode both installed does not list any skill twice; the cli test suite covers the new provider entry and agent dialect; and uninstall removes `.zcode/`.

title: Feature enable order changes the bytes of the installed add.plan
tldr: Enabling tdd-pipeline and qa-pipeline in different orders produces different add.plan files; the installed command should not depend on the order features were switched on.
notes: **Found during delivery 0005B, reproduced without the board feature.** tdd-pipeline and qa-pipeline anchor their step-list sections on the SAME anchor line of add.plan: the two marker pairs sit back to back at framwork/.codeadd/commands/add.plan.md:99-102, right after "- 7.4: Frontend Specialist". Whichever feature is enabled LAST lands FIRST.

**Observed:** enable tdd>qa>docs versus the reverse order swaps "STEP 9.0: QA-Spec subagent" and "STEP 8: Test-Spec subagent". STEP 8 (tdd) should always read before STEP 9.0 (qa), whatever the order.

**Why the suite misses it:** injection-exclusivity.integration.test.js:462, "reversed enable order still lands every full block exactly once", asserts that every block landed, never that the bytes match between the two orders.

**Where the fix likely lives:** cli/src/injection-core.js groups sibling sections by anchor (groupPointsByAnchor, line 160) and applies them bottom-up (applyInjectionToContent, line 180). Sections of DIFFERENT features sharing one anchor need a deterministic order that does not depend on which was already in the file.
**board-feature.test.js L6.4 works around it on purpose:** it keeps the other features in one fixed order so it tests the board feature alone, and says why in a comment. Widen it once this is fixed.
done_when: Enabling tdd-pipeline and qa-pipeline in either order produces a byte-identical add.plan with the tdd step before the qa step, and a test asserts byte equality between the two orders rather than only that every block landed.

title: Board layout that fits the six default columns on a 1080px desktop
tldr: Show every default board column on a 1080px screen without scrolling the row sideways.
notes: Found in delivery 0005B (board pipeline phase statuses), checkpoint 4. The shipped phase model puts six columns on the board by default (seven with ?column=dropped). With the 15rem column floor from the palette delivery (F13), four fit 1080px (~246px each) and six do not (~158px each), so Review and Done only appear by scrolling the column row.

The user chose on 2026-09-23 to ship the six columns with the ROW scrolling and to treat the layout as its own delivery. board/e2e/board.spec.ts L4.5 was rewritten to assert the page never scrolls sideways and every column is reachable along the row.

F13 equal-share sizing was reverted twice on 2026-09-23 by a user looking at a real board, so the fix is a layout decision (narrower cards, collapsing empty columns, a second row, a denser card), not just lowering the floor.
done_when: At 1080px, /board with the shipped definitions shows all six default columns with no row scroll, and board.spec L4.5 asserts that again.
